explanation: Drawings by the Danish traveller Frederic Norden, made in the 1730s, already show it noseless. Chisel marks suggest the nose was deliberately prised off centuries before Napoleon arrived in 1798.

claims.text: Napoleon's soldiers did not shoot the nose off the Great Sphinx; it was already missing before the French expedition of 1798.
Frederic Louis Norden, a Danish explorer, drew the Sphinx without its nose in the 1730s.
Tool marks on the Sphinx's face suggest the nose was deliberately prised off.
The nose was removed centuries before 1798; the historian al-Maqrizi blamed damage to the face on an iconoclast in 1378.
